outcome.headline: An unseen planet pulls Kepler-88 b: roughly 22.3 days and 244 Earth masses, found from transit times alone. It forecasts the later transits to 15 min; the best simple law misses by 200 min.
outcome.action: Confirm with radial velocities, or schedule transit observations from the N-body forecast.

checked_against.name: companion period
checked_against.source: Nesvorny et al. 2013 (later confirmed by radial velocities)

outcome.confidence: one solution of a family: the fit's formal errors (± 0.007 d, ± 10 Earth masses) are too small, since the published period is 11 of them away (0.3%); in timing data the companion's mass trades off against its eccentricity. Published: 22.3383 d, 215.9 ± 7.6 Earth masses.
limits: held-out chi-square 14.9 per transit is above the 4 every law must meet: the timing errors (about 3 min) are smaller than what this fit explains
